chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When it is the Day of 'Arafah, Allah, the Exalted, looks toward the visitors of the grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and says to them, 'Continue (with good deeds), for I have forgiven you.' Then He directs His attention to the people in 'Arafat.

key_terms.اسْتَأْنِفُوا: Continue/Resume (imperative plural, implying continuing in worship or good deeds)
key_terms.زُوَّارِ: Visitors (plural of zahir, specifically referring to pilgrims/visitors of shrines)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat, the plain where pilgrims stand during Hajj
key_terms.قَبْرِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Abu Abdillah al-Husayn (Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of 'Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, a key day in Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn's grave on the Day of 'Arafah?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes the Day of 'Arafah as a unique occasion where divine mercy is first extended to the pilgrims of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) before being directed toward the pilgrims in Mecca, emphasizing the preeminence of his shrine. This sequence underscores the concept of *isti'naf* (renewal) of forgiveness, linking the earthly act of ziyarah with the celestial events of the Hajj season. It serves as a powerful incentive for believers to prioritize visiting Karbala on this day, viewing it as a direct conduit to divine pardon.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan (ibn Aḥmad) ibn Walīd narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid Al-Barqi, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

On the Day of ‘Arafah, Allāh, the Exalted, looks toward the Zuwwār of the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Ḥusain (a.s.) and says, “Continue with (good) deeds for I have forgiven you.” Thereafter, He attends to the people in ‘Arafāt.
